t: The authority provided by section 2011 of title 38, United States Code, shall continue in effect through the date specified in section 106(3) of this division.

fable.w: This section only extends the duration of an existing statutory authority through a date set elsewhere in the division. It does not provide for consultation, a hearing, a comment period, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The one tempting reading is that the underlying title 38 authority (a grant program) involves outside entities, but applying for grants is not participation and nothing in this text creates an outside-party process.
fable.s: The authority provided by section 2011 of title 38, United States Code, shall continue in effect through the date specified in section 106(3) of this division.

opus.w: This section only extends an existing statutory authority to a set date. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Reading in participation through the referenced grant program fails because grant applications are excluded from the definition, and the text itself describes no outside-party process.
opus.s: The authority provided by section 2011 of title 38, United States Code, shall continue in effect through the date specified in section 106(3) of this division.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking.** The tempting reading is that because 38 U.S.C. 2011 (the homeless veterans grant and per diem program) involves outside organizations, extending it counts as participation. That fails for two reasons. First, the section itself only extends a statutory authority to a date and describes no process involving outsiders. Second, even the underlying program is about grant applications, which the definition excludes.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely extends the duration of existing statutory authority. It does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards, state consultation, or rights to sue. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The authority provided by section 2011 of title 38, United States Code, shall continue in effect through the date specified in section 106(3) of this division.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might assume that "section 2011 of title 38" involves participation because it is a substantive statute, but the text provided here does not describe any process, only the continuation of authority. Without evidence of outside involvement in the text itself, we cannot label it "Yes". The text is purely administrative regarding the duration of authority.
